Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Monrovia, Liberia, is one of Nigeria's most important diplomatic missions managing special relationship with West African neighbor. Located in Monrovia, Liberia's capital named after US President Monroe, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Nigeria holds extraordinary status in Liberia stemming from Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping intervention that ended Liberia's devastating civil wars (1989-1996, 1999-2003). Nigerian soldiers made supreme sacrifice with thousands of casualties bringing peace and ending Charles Taylor's brutal regime. Grateful Liberians remember Nigerian peacekeeping heroism. Nigerian traders now dominate Liberian commercial sectors creating economic dependence. Both are English-speaking ECOWAS members with deep ties. Ellen Johnson Sirleaf's presidency (2006-2018) rebuilt Liberia; George Weah (former footballer) leads currently. Post-war reconstruction continues with Nigerian business involvement. Historical ties date to freed American slaves founding Liberia. The mission enjoys privileged status leveraging peacekeeping legacy, protects dominant Nigerian trader community and advances regional integration.

**Core Mandate:** To represent Nigeria's special relationship with Liberia, leverage peacekeeping sacrifice legacy, protect dominant trader community, support reconstruction and advance regional integration.

**Statutory Functions:**

(b) Leverage Nigerian ECOMOG peacekeeping sacrifice that ended Liberia's civil wars

(s) Facilitate frequent high-level visits between Nigerian and Liberian leadership
(t) Advance Nigeria's interests in peacekeeping legacy recognition, regional stability and ECOWAS leadership through special Liberia relationship

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Moscow, Russian Federation, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Russia. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in N'Djamena, Chad, is one of Nigeria's most strategically critical diplomatic missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Chad. Located in N'Djamena, Chad's capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages absolutely crucial security relationship with northern neighbor. Chad is Nigeria's indispensable partner in fighting Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorism around Lake Chad Basin. Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) headquarters in N'Djamena coordinates regional counterterrorism with Nigerian, Chadian, Nigerien, Cameroonian forces. Chad's military strength (arguably Sahel's best army) provides critical support against insurgents. Déby dynasty ruled Chad (Idriss Déby 1990-2021, Mahamat Déby since 2021 coup) with military prowess. Nigeria and Chad share Lake Chad waters and borders. Nigerian refugees fled to Chad from Boko Haram violence. Chad is oil producer and Sahel security anchor despite chronic instability. French military presence in Chad affects regional dynamics. The mission coordinates vital counterterrorism, manages Lake Chad Basin security, facilitates MNJTF operations and maintains critical security partnership.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Niamey, Niger Republic, is one of Nigeria's most strategically critical diplomatic missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in immediate northern neighbor. Located in Niamey, Niger's capital on Niger River, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages absolutely vital relationship given 1,497 km shared border and security interdependence. Both countries face existential terrorism threat from Boko Haram/ISWAP and Islamic State affiliates in Lake Chad Basin and Sahel. Multinational Joint Task Force coordinates counterterrorism with Niger as critical partner. Nigerian refugees fled Boko Haram violence into Niger. Cross-border ethnic ties connect Nigerian and Nigerien communities. Niger is Sahel's poorest country but strategically located. Recent military coups (2023) ended democratic governance complicating relations. French military operated from Niger bases. Uranium production makes Niger significant. ECOWAS and regional integration links both countries. The mission coordinates critical counterterrorism, manages border security, facilitates MNJTF operations and maintains vital security partnership despite Niger's political instability.

Nigeria-Niger Joint Commission (NNJC) in Niamey represents specialized bilateral cooperation mechanism between Nigeria and Niger. The Joint Commission coordinates specific bilateral programs and agreements implementation beyond regular diplomatic functions. Manages technical cooperation in border management, water resources (Lake Chad, Niger River), security coordination, trade facilitation and development projects. Joint Commission institutionalizes Nigeria-Niger partnership addressing cross-border challenges requiring coordinated responses. Facilitates ministerial-level meetings and specialized working groups on sectors like agriculture, security, customs, energy and infrastructure. The facility ensures continuous coordination on shared interests between neighbors with deeply interconnected populations, security challenges and economic systems requiring dedicated cooperation mechanisms beyond standard diplomatic channels.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Ottawa, Canada, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Canada. Located in Ottawa, Canada's capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with G7 developed country and Commonwealth member. Substantial Nigerian diaspora (over 100,000) includes highly skilled professionals, students, permanent residents and refugees. Canada's immigration system attracts Nigerian doctors, engineers, IT professionals and academics. Many Nigerian students study in Canadian universities. Canada provides development assistance to Nigeria. Both countries are Commonwealth members and major oil producers. Canadian mining companies invest in Nigerian mineral sector. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Burkina Faso. Located in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso's capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with Sahel neighbor facing severe terrorism crisis. Burkina Faso under military government (2022 coups) battles jihadist insurgency from multiple groups including JNIM (al-Qaeda affiliate) and Islamic State affiliates controlling large territories. Over 2 million displaced by violence. Nigerian traders operate despite insecurity. Thomas Sankara's revolutionary legacy (1983-1987) remains influential. Both are ECOWAS members. The mission monitors terrorism spillover risks, protects Nigerian traders, coordinates regional security, facilitates ECOWAS mediation and maintains presence despite deteriorating security.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Pretoria, South Africa, is one of Nigeria's most important but contentious diplomatic missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in South Africa. Located in Pretoria, South Africa's administrative capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages complex relationship between Africa's two largest economies and continental rival powers. South Africa experiences periodic xenophobic violence specifically targeting Nigerian nationals, killing dozens and destroying Nigerian businesses. Nigerian traders dominate certain sectors angering South Africans facing unemployment. Rivalry exists over continental leadership, with Nigeria leading West Africa/ECOWAS while South Africa leads Southern Africa/SADC. Both compete for African Union influence. However, substantial economic complementarities exist. South African companies (MTN, Shoprite) invest heavily in Nigeria. The mission coordinates on xenophobia protection, manages continental rivalry, promotes economic cooperation, facilitates BRICS engagement and navigates Nigeria-South Africa tensions while maintaining Africa's two largest economies partnership.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Pyongyang, North Korea, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Rabat, Morocco, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Kingdom of Morocco. Kainji National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and wildlife in northwestern Nigeria. Located across Niger, Kwara and Kebbi States covering approximately 5,341 square kilometers in two sectors (Borgu and Zugurma), operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Houses significant wildlife including elephants, hippopotamus, buffalo, various antelopes (roan, kob, hartebeest), lions, leopards, baboons and over 350 bird species. Borgu sector adjoins Benin's W National Park forming transboundary conservation complex. Faces threats from poaching, cattle grazing, illegal fishing in park waters and human encroachment. Tourism infrastructure limited but includes game viewing and safari camps. Park management involves anti-poaching patrols, habitat conservation, community engagement and sustainable tourism. Collaborates with Benin and Niger on transboundary wildlife conservation. Critical for northwestern Nigeria biodiversity protection and eco-tourism potential.

Kamuku National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and ecosystems in northwestern Nigeria. Located in Kaduna and Niger States covering approximately 1,121 square kilometers, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Houses wildlife including various antelopes, monkeys, baboons, hyenas and bird species. Protects water catchment areas for rivers feeding communities. Faces severe threats from illegal logging, charcoal production, poaching, farmland encroachment and gold mining activities destroying habitats. Mining activities particularly damaging with illegal miners operating within park. Park management severely constrained by limited resources, inadequate rangers and encroachment pressure from surrounding communities. Requires urgent intervention preventing total degradation. Collaborates with Kaduna and Niger State governments on conservation. Demonstrates challenges facing Nigerian national parks from human pressure and inadequate enforcement. King's College Lagos is prestigious federal government college and unity school. Located on Lagos Island, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Established in 1909 during colonial period, King's College is among Nigeria's oldest and most prestigious secondary schools. Provides boarding education promoting national integration. Prepares students for WAEC and NECO examinations with consistently high performance. mda_name: 557. LAGOS INTERNATIONAL TRADE FAIR COMPLEX MANAGEMENT BOARD
mandate_description:

Located in Badagry Expressway, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. The Complex provides permanent exhibition halls, outdoor display areas and facilities for trade fairs, exhibitions and commercial events. Hosts annual Lagos International Trade Fair attracting thousands of exhibitors and visitors showcasing products, services and business opportunities. Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) is premier federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. Located in Idi-Araba, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Health and affiliated with University of Lagos (UNILAG). Lake Chad Research Institute (LCRI) Maiduguri is federal agricultural research institution conducting research on Lake Chad Basin agriculture, fisheries and natural resources. Located in Maiduguri, Borno State in northeastern Nigeria, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Conducts fisheries research on Lake Chad fish species, fishing practices and aquaculture. Researches livestock production in pastoral communities. Legal Aid Council of Nigeria is federal agency providing free legal services to indigent citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Headquartered in Abuja with offices in all 36 states and FCT, operating under Federal Ministry of Justice per Legal Aid Act 2011. Operates Legal Aid clinics in courts, prisons and communities. Represents accused persons facing serious criminal charges who cannot afford lawyers. Provides legal services in civil matters including land disputes, family law, employment and consumer rights. Offers legal advice and counseling to indigent citizens. mda_name: 563. LOWER BENUE RIVER BASIN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (LBRBDA)
mandate_description:
Lower Benue River Basin Development Authority (LBRBDA) is federal agency managing water resources, irrigation and agricultural development in Lower Benue River Basin. Headquartered in Makurdi covering Benue, Kogi, Nasarawa, Cross River, Ebonyi, Enugu and Anambra States, operating under Federal Ministry of Water Resources. Established as one of Nigeria's 12 River Basin Development Authorities. The basin includes Lower Benue River and tributaries. LBRBDA develops irrigation schemes supporting dry season farming. Constructs and operates small/medium dams for irrigation water supply. Manages water distribution to farmers and communities. Supports rice, vegetables and yam production through irrigation. Provides flood control infrastructure. Conducts hydrological studies and water resources assessment. Develops fadama (floodplain) irrigation exploiting seasonal water availability. Provides agricultural extension services to irrigated farmers. Faces challenges from flooding (Benue experiences major floods), inadequate infrastructure maintenance and farmer participation. Benue River's significant discharge creates both irrigation opportunities and flood risks requiring integrated management.

Maritime Academy of Nigeria Oron is premier federal maritime training institution providing education for seafarers and maritime professionals. Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Board (MRTB) is statutory regulatory body overseeing physiotherapy, occupational therapy and other rehabilitation professions. Registers qualified rehabilitation therapists meeting educational requirements. Accredits physiotherapy, occupational therapy and rehabilitation training programs. Conducts professional qualifying examinations. Issues practicing licenses. Enforces professional conduct and ethics in rehabilitation services. Investigates professional misconduct. Imposes disciplinary sanctions. Monitors continuing professional development. Promotes quality rehabilitation services for patients with disabilities, injuries and chronic conditions. Collaborates with rehabilitation facilities, teaching hospitals and professional associations. Addresses challenges from inadequate rehabilitation services, limited trained therapists and public awareness gaps. Metallurgical Training Institute Onitsha is specialized federal technical training institution providing metallurgy and metal working skills education. Located in Onitsha, Anambra State in southeastern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Mines and Steel Development. Established to train metallurgists, welders, fabricators and metal workers supporting Nigeria's steel and metallurgical industries. Provides metal fabrication and sheet metal working training. Offers foundry technology and metal casting training. Teaches metallurgical testing, quality control and materials science. Provides practical hands-on training in workshops. Trains technicians for steel plants, fabrication workshops and manufacturing industries. Supports Ajaokuta Steel Company and steel industry manpower needs. Conducts skills training for artisans and technicians. Collaborates with steel companies, manufacturing firms and technical colleges. Faces challenges from limited equipment, inadequate funding and steel industry underdevelopment. Critical for steel sector development and metallurgical skills in southeastern Nigeria's industrial economy.

mda_name: 570. MICHAEL IMODU INSTITUTE OF LABOUR STUDIES
mandate_description:
Michael Imodu Institute of Labour Studies is federal training and research institution for labor studies, industrial relations and trade unionism. Located in Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. Named after Michael Imoudu, prominent Nigerian labor leader. Established to provide training, research and capacity building for labor movement, trade unions and industrial relations practitioners. Conducts training programs for trade union leaders, shop stewards and labor organizers. Provides industrial relations education for employers, workers and government officials. Conducts research on labor issues, collective bargaining, workers' rights and employment relations. Offers certificate and diploma programs in labor studies. Trains labor inspectors and ministry of labour officials. Provides negotiation and conflict resolution skills training. Conducts workers' education promoting labor rights awareness. Researches Nigerian labor history and trade union movements. Collaborates with ILO, trade unions (NLC, TUC) and international labor education institutions. Addresses challenges from declining union membership, changing work patterns and labor movement fragmentation. Critical for industrial harmony, collective bargaining effectiveness and workers' rights protection.

mda_name: 571. MICHAEL OKPARA UNIVERSITY OF AGRICULTURE, UMUDIKE (MOUAU)
mandate_description:
Michael Okpara University of Agriculture Umudike (MOUAU) is specialized federal university focusing on agricultural education, research and development. Located in Umudike, Abia State in southeastern Nigeria, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Established in 1992 and named after Dr. Michael Okpara, former Premier of Eastern Nigeria and agricultural champion. MOUAU focuses exclusively on agriculture, agricultural sciences and related disciplines. Offers undergraduate and postgraduate programs in agronomy, animal science, soil science, agricultural economics, agricultural engineering, food science, forestry and fisheries. Conducts agricultural research on crop production, livestock, soil management and agricultural technologies. Operates teaching and research farms demonstrating improved agricultural practices. Focuses on southeastern Nigeria agroecological zone crops including cassava, yam, cocoa, oil palm and vegetables. Conducts extension services training farmers. Researches sustainable agriculture, climate-smart farming and agricultural mechanization. Collaborates with IITA, agricultural research institutes and international agricultural universities. Addresses food security, rural development and agricultural transformation. Produces agricultural graduates and expertise supporting Nigeria's agricultural sector development.

Military Pension Board is federal agency managing pensions and retirement benefits for Nigerian Armed Forces personnel. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Defence. Established to administer pension payments, gratuities and death benefits for retired military personnel, veterans and dependents of deceased service members. Processes retirement benefits for Army, Navy and Air Force retirees. Calculates pension entitlements based on rank, years of service and retirement conditions. Pays monthly pensions to retired military personnel. Processes gratuities (lump sum retirement benefits) upon discharge. Manages death benefits and pensions for widows/orphans of deceased soldiers. Addresses pension arrears and outstanding payments. Maintains database of military retirees and pensioners. Verifies pensioners through biometric registration preventing fraud. Collaborates with Defense Headquarters, service branches and PenCom. Faces challenges from pension arrears, inadequate funding, verification difficulties and delayed payments affecting veterans' welfare. Military pension is distinct from contributory pension applying to civilian workers. Critical for military morale, retirement security and honoring service to nation.

Issues mineral exploration licenses, mining leases, small-scale mining licenses and quarrying permits. Maintains comprehensive database of all mineral titles across Nigeria. Prevents overlapping claims through geographic information system (GIS) mapping. Processes applications for mineral rights electronically. Monitors compliance with mineral title conditions. Collects royalties and fees from mining license holders. Provides transparency in mineral rights allocation preventing corruption. Makes mineral title information publicly accessible. Collaborates with mining companies, artisanal miners and state governments. Addresses challenges from illegal mining, artisanal mining formalization and mineral revenue collection. Critical for mining sector regulation, investor confidence and transparent mineral resource governance. Supports Nigeria's solid minerals sector development beyond oil dependence.

Federal Ministry of Defence Headquarters is apex civilian ministry overseeing Nigerian Armed Forces and defense policy. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Defence appointed by President. Provides civilian oversight and political direction for military. Formulates national defense policy and military strategy. Coordinates Army, Navy, Air Force and Defense Intelligence Agency. Manages defense budget allocation across service branches. Coordinates defense diplomacy and military cooperation with foreign countries. Manages defense industries and military production. Oversees military training institutions. Coordinates peacekeeping troop contributions to UN and AU missions. Supervises veterans' affairs and military welfare. Coordinates civil-military relations. Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs Headquarters is apex ministry managing Nigeria's foreign policy, diplomacy and international relations. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Foreign Affairs appointed by President. Formulates and implements Nigeria's foreign policy. Federal Ministry of Interior is ministry overseeing internal security agencies, immigration, prisons and civil defense. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Interior appointed by President. Supervises Nigeria Immigration Service controlling borders and immigration. Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources is apex ministry overseeing Nigeria's oil and gas industry and petroleum sector. Located in Abuja, operating under executive branch with Minister of Petroleum Resources (often held by President) and Minister of State. Formulates petroleum policies and regulations. mda_name: 578. MODIBBO ADAMA UNIVERSITY TEACHING HOSPITAL (MAUTH), YOLA
mandate_description:
Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital Yola is federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. National Assembly Management is administrative arm supporting Nigeria's bicameral legislature. Located in Abuja at National Assembly Complex, operating under National Assembly Service Commission. Gashaka Gumti National Park is Nigeria's largest national park protecting biodiversity, wildlife and ecosystems. Located across Taraba and Adamawa States in northeastern Nigeria covering approximately 6,731 square kilometers, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established in 1991 by merging Gashaka and Gumti Game Reserves creating Nigeria's premier wildlife conservation area. The park protects montane forests, savanna, grasslands and Nigeria's highest mountain peak (Chappal Waddi at 2,419 meters). Houses significant biodiversity including chimpanzees, elephants, buffalo, hippopotamus, various antelopes, lions (possibly), leopards and over 500 bird species. Provides critical watershed for Taraba and Benue Rivers. Faces threats from poaching, illegal logging, cattle grazing encroachment and human-wildlife conflict. Tourism potential largely undeveloped due to remoteness and infrastructure challenges. Park management involves conservation, anti-poaching patrols, research, community engagement and sustainable tourism development. Collaborates with local communities on conservation and livelihood programs.

Geneva Labour Desk Office is specialized Nigerian government office representing Nigeria's labor interests at International Labour Organization (ILO) and UN agencies in Geneva, Switzerland. Geological Survey of Nigeria (GSN) is premier federal geological research institution conducting geological surveys, mineral exploration, geoscience research and providing geological information. Hadejia-Jama'are River Basin Development Authority (HJRBDA) is federal agency managing water resources, irrigation development and agricultural programs in Hadejia-Jama'are river basin. mda_name: 533. INDEPENDENT CORRUPT PRACTICES AND RELATED OFFENCES COMMISSION (ICPC)
mandate_description:
Independent Corrupt Practices and Related Offences Commission (ICPC) is federal anti-corruption agency investigating, preventing and prosecuting corruption in public sector. Headquartered in Abuja with zonal offices nationwide, operating as independent statutory body under ICPC Act 2000. Established to combat corruption complementing Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). ICPC focuses on corruption prevention, public sector corruption, abuse of office, gratification and system reforms strengthening integrity. Investigates corruption allegations against public officials including bribery, fraud, abuse of office and illicit enrichment. Prosecutes corruption cases in courts. Conducts Corruption Risk Assessments and System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities in MDAs. Promotes ethics, integrity and anti-corruption education. Monitors Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking implementation. Receives and investigates petitions from citizens. Operates independently though faces challenges from political interference, inadequate funding, lengthy prosecutions and weak conviction rates. Collaborates with EFCC, CCB, CCT and international anti-corruption agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To prevent, investigate and prosecute corruption in public sector; strengthen integrity systems; promote ethics; and advance anti-corruption reforms in Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Investigate corruption, bribery and abuse of office allegations in public sector
(b) Prosecute corrupt public officials in courts for corruption offenses
(c) Prevent corruption through system reforms and integrity strengthening
(d) Conduct Corruption Risk Assessments in Ministries, Departments and Agencies
(e) Perform System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities
(f) Monitor Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking fund utilization
(g) Receive, investigate and act on corruption petitions from citizens
(h) Investigate gratification, bribery and illicit enrichment by public officials
(i) Prosecute abuse of office, fraud and corruption in procurement
(j) Promote ethics, integrity and anti-corruption values in public service
(k) Conduct anti-corruption education in schools, MDAs and communities
(l) Enforce asset declaration requirements for public officials
(m) Collaborate with EFCC on joint anti-corruption operations
(n) Coordinate with Code of Conduct Bureau on asset verification
(o) Provide technical assistance to MDAs on corruption prevention
(p) Conduct public enlightenment campaigns on corruption reporting
(q) Collaborate with civil society organizations on anti-corruption advocacy
(r) Coordinate with international anti-corruption agencies and conventions
(s) Recommend policy and legislative reforms strengthening anti-corruption frameworks
(t) Advance Nigeria's anti-corruption fight through prevention, investigation, prosecution and systemic reforms reducing corruption in public institutions

Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is Nigeria's electoral management body conducting elections, voter registration and electoral processes. Headquartered in Abuja with offices in all 36 states and 774 Local Governments, operating as constitutionally established independent commission. Mandated by 1999 Constitution and Electoral Act to organize, conduct and supervise elections for President, National Assembly, Governors and State Assemblies. INEC registers voters through Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) maintaining national voter register. Conducts elections including presidential, gubernatorial, National Assembly, State Assembly and Area Council elections. Registers political parties and monitors party activities. Delimits constituencies for electoral purposes. Conducts voter education promoting electoral participation. Procures electoral materials including ballot papers, result sheets and Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) technology. Recruits and trains ad hoc election staff. Announces election results and issues Certificates of Return to winners. Faces challenges from electoral violence, logistical difficulties, result manipulation allegations, voter apathy and political interference despite constitutional independence.

**Core Mandate:** To organize, conduct and supervise free, fair and credible elections; register voters and political parties; promote electoral participation; and strengthen Nigeria's democracy through professional electoral management.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Organize, conduct and supervise presidential elections every four years
(b) Conduct National Assembly elections for Senate and House of Representatives
(c) Organize gubernatorial elections in 36 states
(d) Conduct State Houses of Assembly elections across Nigeria
(e) Organize Area Council elections in Federal Capital Territory
(f) Register eligible Nigerian citizens as voters through Continuous Voter Registration
(g) Maintain and update National Register of Voters
(h) Register political parties meeting constitutional requirements
(i) Monitor political party activities and campaign finances
(j) Delimit constituencies for National Assembly and State Assemblies
(k) Conduct voter education and public enlightenment on electoral processes
(l) Procure electoral materials including ballot papers and result sheets
(m) Deploy Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for voter authentication
(n) Recruit, train and deploy ad hoc election staff including Presiding Officers
(o) Collate and announce election results at ward, LGA, state and national levels
(p) Issue Certificates of Return to elected officials
(q) Address electoral offenses including vote buying and ballot stuffing
(r) Conduct bye-elections and re-run elections as ordered by courts
(s) Collaborate with security agencies on election security
(t) Advance Nigeria's democracy through credible electoral processes, transparent result management and continuous electoral reforms strengthening public confidence in democratic governance

Industrial Arbitration Panel (IAP) is specialized tribunal adjudicating industrial disputes between employers and workers in Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment per Trade Disputes Act. Established to resolve industrial disputes through arbitration avoiding prolonged strikes disrupting economy. IAP hears trade disputes referred by Minister of Labour when conciliation fails. Adjudicates disputes on wages, conditions of employment, termination, unfair labor practices and collective bargaining disagreements. Panel comprises neutral arbitrators with labor law expertise. Conducts hearings, examines evidence, hears parties and issues binding awards. Awards are enforceable in National Industrial Court. Provides faster dispute resolution than courts. Addresses disputes in critical sectors including oil/gas, banking, aviation, health and education. Promotes industrial harmony and peaceful labor relations. Faces challenges from parties' non-compliance with awards, legal challenges to jurisdiction and limited enforcement mechanisms. Complements National Industrial Court and labor ministry conciliation services.

**Core Mandate:** To adjudicate industrial disputes through arbitration, issue binding awards, promote industrial harmony and resolve employer-worker conflicts in Nigerian labor market.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Adjudicate industrial disputes referred by Minister of Labour and Employment
(b) Hear trade disputes between employers and workers/unions
(c) Arbitrate disputes on wages, salaries and remuneration
(d) Resolve conflicts over conditions of employment and workplace rights
(e) Adjudicate wrongful termination and unfair dismissal disputes
(f) Address unfair labor practices by employers or unions
(g) Resolve collective bargaining disagreements
(h) Conduct arbitration hearings in industrial dispute cases
(i) Examine evidence, witness testimonies and parties' submissions

(k) Enforce awards through National Industrial Court mechanisms
(l) Prevent or end strikes through binding dispute resolution
(m) Promote industrial peace and harmonious labor relations
(n) Address disputes in critical sectors (oil/gas, banking, aviation, health)
(o) Provide expedited alternative to lengthy court litigation
(p) Protect workers' rights while balancing employers' interests
(q) Interpret collective agreements and employment contracts
(r) Coordinate with Ministry of Labour on labor dispute management
(s) Collaborate with National Industrial Court on enforcement
(t) Advance industrial harmony, prevent disruptive strikes and resolve employer-worker conflicts protecting Nigeria's economic stability and workers' rights

Industrial Training Fund (ITF) is premier federal skills development agency providing vocational training, skills acquisition and human capital development for Nigerian workforce. Headquartered in Jos, Plateau State with Area Offices and Model Skills Training Centres nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. Established by ITF Act 2011 to promote acquisition of skills in industry and commerce. ITF collects 1% levy from companies with 5+ employees (payroll ≥N50 million annually) financing training programs. Provides skills training in technical trades, industrial skills, entrepreneurship and modern technologies. Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) is federal regulatory agency overseeing Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and infrastructure concessions in Nigeria. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission Act 2005 under Presidency. Established to regulate PPP projects ensuring value for money, fiscal sustainability and public interest protection. ICRC provides technical support to MDAs developing PPP projects. Conducts Outline Business Case (OBC) and Full Business Case (FBC) reviews approving projects. Issues Compliance Certificates for PPP projects meeting regulatory requirements. Develops guidelines, regulations and standard templates for PPP contracts. Conducts Value for Money assessments ensuring taxpayers benefit from PPPs. Reviews unsolicited proposals from private sector. Addresses fiscal risks from government guarantees in PPPs. Promotes transparent, competitive PPP procurement. Has reviewed major projects including Lekki-Epe Expressway, Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 2 and others. Faces challenges from limited PPP financing, capacity gaps and slow project approvals.

mda_name: 538. INSTITUTE FOR PEACE AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION (IPCR)
mandate_description:
Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR) is federal agency promoting peace, preventing conflicts and mediating disputes across Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Office of Secretary to Government of the Federation. Established in 2000 to address Nigeria's numerous conflicts including ethnic, religious, communal, land and political disputes. IPCR conducts conflict early warning monitoring potential flashpoints. Provides mediation and dialogue facilitation in communal conflicts. Conducts peace education and training on conflict resolution. Develops National Policy on Peacebuilding and Conflict Management. Operates Peace and Conflict Review magazine. Trains security personnel, traditional rulers, religious leaders and youth in conflict prevention. Conducts research on conflict drivers and peace interventions. Mediates farmer-herder conflicts, communal clashes, electoral violence and boundary disputes. Collaborates with ECOWAS Early Warning System. Provides conflict assessments for government interventions. Organizes peace summits and dialogue forums. Faces challenges from proliferation of conflicts, limited resources, enforcement gaps and political interference in conflict mediation.

**Core Mandate:** To promote peace, prevent conflicts, provide mediation services, conduct peace education and support government conflict resolution efforts across Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**

mda_name: 539. INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND TRAINING (IAR&T), IBADAN
mandate_description:
Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T) Ibadan is federal agricultural research institution conducting research on tropical agriculture, crop production and agricultural technologies. Located at Moor Plantation, Ibadan, Oyo State, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established in 1969 focusing on southwestern Nigeria agroecological zone. IAR&T conducts research on major crops including cassava, maize, yam, cocoa, oil palm, plantain, vegetables and tree crops. Develops improved crop varieties with higher yields, disease resistance and climate adaptation. Researches soil fertility management, integrated pest management and sustainable farming systems. Conducts agroforestry and soil conservation research. Develops agricultural technologies and farming practices. Trains farmers, extension agents and agricultural students. Multiplies and distributes improved seeds and planting materials. Operates demonstration farms showcasing research results. Publishes research findings and technical bulletins. Collaborates with IITA, universities and international agricultural research centers. Addresses food security, climate change adaptation and sustainable agriculture in southwestern Nigeria and beyond.

**Core Mandate:** To conduct agricultural research, develop improved crop varieties, generate agricultural technologies and provide training supporting food security and agricultural development in Nigeria.

Institute for Agricultural Research (IAR) Zaria is premier federal agricultural research institution conducting research on crops, livestock and agricultural systems in northern Nigeria. Located at Ahmadu Bello University, Samaru, Zaria, Kaduna State, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established in 1922 (originally as research station), IAR is Nigeria's oldest agricultural research institute. Focuses on savanna agroecology covering northern Nigeria. Conducts research on sorghum, millet, groundnut, cowpea, rice, cotton, sesame and other dryland crops. Develops drought-tolerant crop varieties for semi-arid regions. Researches livestock production including cattle, small ruminants and poultry. Conducts integrated crop-livestock systems research. Develops farming systems for sustainable Sahel agriculture. Researches soil and water conservation for semi-arid environments. Provides technical advice on agricultural policies. Trains farmers, extension workers and students. Multiplies and distributes seeds of improved varieties. Collaborates with ICRISAT, IITA and international dryland agriculture research centers. Addresses food security, drought resilience and poverty in northern Nigeria's agricultural economy.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Tunis, Tunisia, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Tunisian Republic. Located in Tunis, Tunisia's capital on Mediterranean coast and birthplace of Arab Spring uprisings, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with North African moderate democracy. Tunisia's 2011 Jasmine Revolution sparked Arab Spring across Middle East and North Africa. Limited Nigerian community includes students attracted by Arab-African culture, traders and migrants using Tunisia as transit point attempting Mediterranean crossing to Europe. Tunisia maintained democracy better than other Arab Spring countries but faces severe economic challenges, youth unemployment and political instability. Nigerian migrants detained in Tunisia while attempting European entry. Both countries cooperate in African Union. Tunisia has agricultural expertise particularly olive production and tourism experience. Historic Carthage heritage provides cultural richness. The mission addresses irregular migration transit issues, promotes bilateral trade, coordinates AU engagement, protects limited diaspora and maintains North African presence while supporting Tunisia's fragile democratic experiment.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission to Vatican City (Holy See) is a specialized diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria to Vatican City State and global Catholic Church. Located in Vatican City, world's smallest sovereign state within Rome, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's religious diplomatic relationship with Catholic Church headquarters and Pope. Nigeria has Africa's largest Catholic population with approximately 30 million Catholics representing about 15% of Nigerian population concentrated in southern regions. Vatican exercises significant influence over Nigerian Catholics and provides humanitarian assistance to Nigeria. Nigerian Cardinals including Francis Arinze participate in Papal elections and Vatican leadership. Vatican addresses Nigerian religious conflicts, Boko Haram persecution of Christians and promotes inter-religious dialogue between Nigerian Christians and Muslims. Pope Francis has condemned Boko Haram attacks on Nigerian Christians. Vatican City hosts Nigerian Catholic pilgrims visiting St. Peter's Basilica. The mission coordinates religious diplomacy, addresses Christian persecution in northern Nigeria, facilitates Vatican humanitarian assistance, protects Nigerian pilgrims and represents Nigerian Catholic interests to global Church leadership.

Limited Nigerian diaspora includes students and professionals. Austria is wealthy EU member with strong economy and culture. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Warsaw, Poland, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Poland. Located in Warsaw, Poland's capital rebuilt after WWII devastation, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages limited bilateral engagement with Central European EU member experiencing rapid economic growth. Growing Nigerian community includes students attracted by affordable EU education quality and migrants. Poland played crucial unexpected role during Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, serving as primary evacuation route for thousands of Nigerian students fleeing Ukraine through Polish border crossings. Polish authorities and citizens provided humanitarian assistance to evacuating Nigerian students. Some Nigerian irregular migrants transit Poland attempting Western European entry. Poland's economic transformation from communism to emerging EU economy creates opportunities. However, Poland has conservative Law and Justice government and some anti-immigrant sentiment in society. Limited Polish investment in Nigeria. The mission protects growing diaspora, coordinates Ukraine border crossing support during evacuations, promotes educational cooperation, facilitates minimal trade and maintains Central European diplomatic presence despite limited bilateral engagement.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Washington DC, United States, is one of Nigeria's most strategically critical diplomatic missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in United States of America. Located in Washington DC, US capital and global superpower headquarters, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's single most important bilateral relationship outside Africa with world's only superpower and largest economy. Massive Nigerian diaspora exceeding 400,000 makes United States home to largest Nigerian community outside Nigeria, concentrated in Texas, Maryland, New York, California and Georgia. US is Nigeria's major trading partner, largest foreign investor and significant development assistance provider through USAID. Hundreds of thousands of Nigerian students study across American universities. US military cooperation includes equipment, training and intelligence support for Nigerian counter-Boko Haram operations. However, relations experience periodic strains from US human rights concerns about Nigerian security forces, visa restrictions affecting Nigerians, terrorism designation debates and President Trump's reported 2018 "shithole countries" comment including Nigeria. The mission coordinates vast bilateral relations spanning security cooperation, trade and investment, massive diaspora engagement, development assistance while addressing contentions and managing this crucial superpower relationship affecting Nigerian interests globally.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Windhoek, Namibia, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Namibia. Located in Windhoek, Namibia's capital in Southern African plateau region, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages limited bilateral engagement with sparsely populated Southern African country (population 2.5 million). Minimal Nigerian community present. Namibia is stable multi-party democracy with significant mineral wealth including uranium (world's third-largest producer), diamonds, zinc and copper, plus growing tourism sector. Both countries cooperate in African Union and SADC-ECOWAS partnerships linking West and Southern African regional organizations. Nigeria supported Namibia's liberation struggle against South African apartheid occupation during 1970s-1980s when South Africa illegally occupied territory. Namibia gained independence in 1990 following Nigerian diplomatic support in UN and African forums. Namibia demonstrates good governance, low corruption and democratic stability under SWAPO party. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Yaoundé, Cameroon, is Nigeria's primary diplomatic mission to Republic of Cameroon serving as embassy headquarters (note: separate consular offices may exist in Buea/Douala). Located in Yaoundé, Cameroon's political capital in central highlands, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages absolutely crucial relationship with major eastern neighbor sharing Africa's sixth-longest international border at 1,690 km. Nigeria-Cameroon relations complicated by decades-long Bakassi Peninsula territorial dispute finally resolved by International Court of Justice in 2002 awarding oil-rich peninsula to Cameroon despite Nigerian occupation, creating painful territorial loss. Both countries cooperate extensively on Lake Chad Basin security operations against Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorism threatening both nations. Significant cross-border trade occurs given shared border. Substantial population movement between countries with cross-border ethnic communities. Nigerian refugees fled to Cameroon during 1967-1970 civil war; currently Cameroonian refugees flee anglophone crisis violence to Nigeria reversing flows. Cameroon's anglophone regions (Northwest and Southwest) face separatist armed conflict affecting border security. The mission coordinates vital security cooperation, manages post-Bakassi relations and resettlement, facilitates extensive cross-border trade, protects Nigerian diaspora and maintains crucial neighbor partnership despite complex historical tensions and ongoing challenges.

Foreign Service Academy (FSA) is Nigeria's premier diplomatic training institution responsible for preparing Nigerian diplomats, foreign service officers and international relations professionals for representing Nigeria globally. Located in Nigeria (specific location may be Abuja or Lagos), operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Academy provides comprehensive professional training for career diplomats including diplomatic protocol, international law, diplomatic practice, multilateral and bilateral negotiation, consular services, trade and economic diplomacy, public diplomacy and specialized area studies. FSA trains entry-level foreign service officers fresh from recruitment, mid-career diplomats requiring professional development and senior officials preparing for ambassadorial postings across Nigeria's 120+ foreign missions worldwide. Curriculum covers UN system operations, African Union engagement, ECOWAS regional integration, crisis management, diaspora engagement, digital diplomacy and cultural representation. The Academy ensures Nigerian diplomats possess professional competence, ethical standards and skills necessary for effectively representing Nigeria's interests across diverse global contexts from Washington to Windhoek, Beijing to Bamako. Coordinates with international diplomatic training institutions and academies worldwide.
